..  _columns-number-properties-scale:

..  confval:: scale
    :name: number-scale
    :TCA path: $GLOBALS['TCA'][$table]['columns'][$field]['config']['scale']
    :type: integer
    :default: 0
    :Scope: Display / Proc.
    :added: 15.0 feature-102217-1787855070

    The number of decimal digits. With the default `0`, the field holds an
    integer. The scale is between `0` and `30`. A value outside this range
    is set to the nearest limit.

    The scale applies wherever the value is handled:

    *   The automatically generated database column is an :sql:`int` for a
        scale of `0`. For a higher scale, it is a :sql:`decimal` with eight
        digits in front of the decimal point, plus the scale. A scale of `6`
        gives a :sql:`decimal(14,6)`.
    *   The :php-short:`\TYPO3\CMS\Core\DataHandling\DataHandler` rounds
        every value it saves to the scale. A column declared with more
        decimal digits in :file:`ext_tables.sql` loses them on the next save.
    *   The input field in the backend form uses the scale as its
        :html:`step` attribute, for example :html:`step="0.000001"` for a
        scale of `6`. Browsers cannot check a step below :html:`1e-18`. For a
        scale above `18`, the field has :html:`step="any"`, and the browser
        does not restrict the value.

    When you lower the scale of an existing field, stored values can have
    more decimal digits than the scale. The backend form shows such a value
    rounded, and the next save of the record stores it rounded. MySQL and
    PostgreSQL round the stored values when the column is changed. SQLite
    keeps decimal values as strings and does not round them.

..  rubric:: Example: Coordinates with six decimal digits

Six decimal digits put a geographic position on a grid of about ten
centimetres:
